messages.subject: Enforcing a constant day time TC
messages.subject_clean: Enforcing a constant day time TC
messages.body_plain:
Good afternoon Mike,

I am very new to NicheMapR and am having a bit of trouble with getting my model to represent natural torpor. I want to mimic the results of a study which shows relatively constant day time temperatures followed by a nightly drop into torpor (doi:10.1098/rsbl.2019.0211). I'm not sure how can I adjust different aspects of torpor to more closely match measured results. I've pasted my code below and am currently using the following parameters:

########### Parameters ############
TC <- 41.9                # Core body temperature (°C)
TC_MAX <- 46              # Maximum core body temperature (°C)
TC_MIN <- 30.4            # Minimum core body temperature (°C)
TC_INC <- 0.22            # Increment of core body temperature elevation (°C)
PCTWET <- 1               # Base skin wetness (%)
PCTWET_MAX <- 5           # Maximum skin wetness (%)
PCTWET_INC <- 0.25        # Increments of skin wetness increase (%)
Q10s <- rep(1, length(TAs))        # The effect of body temperature on metabolic rate,
Q10s[TAs >= TC_MAX] <- 2           # The effect starts above TC_MAX
QBASAL <- 10^(-1.461 + 0.669 * log10(AMASS * 1000))   # Basal heat generation (W)
DELTAR <- 5               # Difference between air temperature and breath (°C)
EXTREF <- 25              # O2 extraction efficiency (%)
PANT_INC <- 0.1           # Increment by which panting is increased
PANT_MAX <- 15            # Maximum panting rate
PANT_MULT <- 1            # Multiplier on basal metabolism at maximum panting level
TORPOR <- 1               # Allows body temperature to drop to TC_MIN
TREGMODE <- 2
endoshade <- 0
#############################################

Here is my endoR loop. I am running it through different feather conditions however that is working well, it is the torpor that needs adjusting:

##############################################
results_list <- list()   # store results for each condition level

ptm <- proc.time()

for (i in seq_along(condition_grid)) {

  # Scale feather density and length
  LHAIRD <- condition_grid[i] * LHAIRD_base
  LHAIRV <- condition_grid[i] * LHAIRV_base
  RHOD   <- condition_grid[i] * RHOD_base
  RHOV   <- condition_grid[i] * RHOV_base

  # Run endoR across all microclimate time steps
  endo.out <- lapply(seq_along(TAs), function(x) {

    # Behavioural ptiloerection based on air temperature
    ptilo <- ptilo_func(TAs[x])

    # Adjust feather depth (ptiloerection)
    ZFURD <- ZFURD_base + (LHAIRD - ZFURD_base) * ptilo
    ZFURV <- ZFURV_base + (LHAIRV - ZFURV_base) * ptilo

    # Run endoR with modified insulation
    endoR(
      # Climate variables
      TA = TAs[x], TAREF = TAREFs[x], TSKY = TSKYs[x], TGRD = TGRDs[x],
      VEL = VELs[x], RH = RHs[x], QSOLR = QSOLRs[x], Z = Zs[x], ELEV = ELEV,
      ABSSB = ABSSB,

      # Constants
      TC = TC, TC_MAX = TC_MAX, AMASS = AMASS, SHAPE = SHAPE,
      SHAPE_B = SHAPE_B, SHAPE_B_MAX = SHAPE_B_MAX,
      PCTWET = PCTWET, PCTWET_INC = PCTWET_INC,
      Q10 = Q10s[x], QBASAL = QBASAL, DELTAR = DELTAR,
      DHAIRD = DHAIRD, DHAIRV = DHAIRV,
      REFLD = REFLD, TC_INC = TC_INC, PANT_INC = PANT_INC,
      PANT_MAX = PANT_MAX, EXTREF = EXTREF, UNCURL = UNCURL,
      SAMODE = SAMODE, PANT_MULT = PANT_MULT, TORPOR = TORPOR,
      SHADE = endoshade, TREGMODE = TREGMODE,

      # Varied Feather Traits
      LHAIRD = LHAIRD,
      LHAIRV = LHAIRV,
      RHOD   = RHOD,
      RHOV   = RHOV,
      ZFURD  = ZFURD,
      ZFURV  = ZFURV
    )
  })

  # Convert list of endoR outputs into a single data frame
  endo_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(endo.out, data.frame))

  # Climate
  daynight <- ifelse(Zs >= 90, "night", "day")

  # Extract heat balance (metabolic rate)
  enbal <- endo_df[, grep("enbal", colnames(endo_df))]
  colnames(enbal) <- gsub("enbal.", "", colnames(enbal))

  # Thermoregulation output
  treg <- endo_df[, grep("treg", colnames(endo_df))]
  colnames(treg) <- gsub("treg\\.", "", colnames(treg))

  # Mass aspects
  masbal <- endo_df[, grep("masbal", colnames(endo_df))]
  colnames(masbal) <- gsub("masbal\\.", "", colnames(masbal))

  # Save results for this condition level
  results_list[[i]] <- data.frame(
    condition = condition_grid[i],
    time_step = seq_along(TAs),
    QGEN = enbal$QGEN,                             # Metabolic energy generated
    TCs = treg$TC,                                 # Core temperature
    H2O = masbal$H2OResp_g + masbal$H2OCut_g,      # Water evaporated (g/hour)
    TFA_D = treg$TFA_D,                            # Dorsal fur surface temperature
    TFA_V = treg$TFA_V,                            # Ventral fur surface temperature
    TskinD = treg$TSKIN_D,                         # Dorsal skin temperature
    TskinV = treg$TSKIN_V,                         # Ventral skin temperature
    Pant = treg$PANT,                              # Panting multiplier
    daynight = daynight                            # Day or night
  )
}

proc.time() - ptm

results_all <- do.call(rbind, results_list)

ggplot(results_all, aes(x = time_step, y = TCs, colour = factor(condition))) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Time step",
    y = "Core Temperature",
    colour = "Feather condition"
  )
#############################################

I hope this is enough to explain my problem, and thank you for your time.
All the best,
Caity

messages.body_plain:
Thank you Mike,

I've added a night time requirement for TORPOR in the following self-contained code. While the animal does drop into torpor at night, the drop is seemingly instant unlike the gradual decrease measured experimentally. I was wondering if there was a way to encode some kind of non-energetic cost of torpor that would prevent the model from immediately maximising it. Otherwise, how would I force the model to consider TORPOR a last resort. Thank you and I hope this code runs!

All the best,
Caity

#############################################################
library(NicheMapR)
library(ggplot2)

# Australian National Botanic Gardens Input
loc <- c(149.1112592, -35.2733684)    # Coordinates
maxshade <- 100                       # Maximum Shade

# Superb fairywren centroid height (m)
Usrhyt <- 0.07

# Running the microclimate models
micro <- micro_global(loc = loc, Usrhyt = Usrhyt, maxshade = maxshade)

metout <- as.data.frame(micro$metout)          # unshaded above-ground conditions
soil <- as.data.frame(micro$soil)              # unshaded below-ground soil temperatures
shadmet <- as.data.frame(micro$shadmet)        # shaded above-ground conditions
shadsoil <- as.data.frame(micro$shadsoil)      # shaded below-ground soil temperatures
dates <- micro$dates

TAs <- metout$TALOC            # air temperatures at height of animal (°C)
TAREFs <- metout$TAREF         # air temperatures at reference height (°C)
TSKYs <- metout$TSKYC          # sky temperatures (°C)
TGRDs <- soil$D0cm             # surface temperatures (°C)
VELs <- metout$VLOC            # wind speeds at animal height (m/s)
RHs <- metout$RHLOC            # relative humidity at animal height (%)
QSOLRs <- metout$SOLR          # solar radiation (W/m2)
Zs <- metout$ZEN               # zenith angle of the sun (degrees)
ELEV <- micro$elev             # elevation (m)
ABSSB <- 1 - micro$REFL        # substrate solar absorptivity (%)

# Morphometric Parameters
AMASS <- 0.0097    # Mass (kg)
ANDENS <- 875     # Flesh density (kg/m^3)
AK1 <- 1          # Initial thermal conductivity of flesh (0.412 - 2.8 W/mK)
SHAPE_B <- 1.01   # Long to short body axis ratio
SHAPE_B_MAX <- 2  # Maximum long to short body axis ratio
UNCURL <- 0.1     # Increment of change between SHAPE_B and SHAPE_B_MAX
SHAPE <- 4        # Shape type (4 = ellipsoid)
SAMODE <- 1       # Geometry (1 = bird)
FATPCT <- 3.6     # Body fat (%)

# Metabolic Parameters and Physiological Responses

TC <- 41.9                # Core body temperature (°C)
TC_MAX <- 46              # Maximum core body temperature (°C)
TC_MIN <- 30.4            # Minimum core body temperature (°C)
TC_INC <- 0.22            # Increment of core body temperature elevation (°C)
PCTWET <- 1               # Base skin wetness (%)
PCTWET_MAX <- 5           # Maximum skin wetness (%)
PCTWET_INC <- 0.25        # Increments of skin wetness increase (%)
Q10s <- rep(1, length(TAs))        # The effect of body temperature on metabolic rate,
Q10s[TAs >= TC_MAX] <- 2           # The effect starts above TC_MAX
QBASAL <- 10^(-1.461 + 0.669 * log10(AMASS * 1000))   # Basal heat generation (W)
DELTAR <- 5               # Difference between air temperature and breath (°C)
EXTREF <- 25              # O2 extraction efficiency (%)
PANT_INC <- 0.1           # Increment by which panting is increased
PANT_MAX <- 15            # Maximum panting rate
PANT_MULT <- 1            # Multiplier on basal metabolism at maximum panting level

# Fixed Feather Properties
DHAIRD <- 0.00003         # Dorsal "hair" diameter (m)
DHAIRV <- 0.00003         # Ventral "hair" diameter (m)
REFLD <- 0.41             # Dorsal fractional reflectivity (0-1)
REFLV <- 0.48             # Ventral fractional reflectivity (0-1)

# Base Feather Properties (adjusted seasonally) !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! CORRECT THESE TO FAIRYWREN VALUES
#ZFURD <- 0.00217               # Dorsal "fur" depth (m) -> will vary with ptiloerection
#ZFURV <- 0.00254               # Ventral "fur" depth (m)  -> will vary with ptiloerection
LHAIRD_base <- 0.01611         # Dorsal "hair" length (m)
LHAIRV_base <- 0.01413         # Ventral "hair" length (m)
RHOD_base <- 5e+07             # Dorsal feather density (m^-2)
RHOV_base <- 5e+07             # Ventral feather density (m^-2)
TREGMODE <- 1                  # Allows dynamic ptiloerection

condition_grid <- seq(0.5, 3.5, by = 0.5) # To cycle through feather conditions

results_list_torpor <- list()   # store results for each condition level

ptm <- proc.time()

for (i in seq_along(condition_grid)) {

  # Scale feather density and length
  LHAIRD <- condition_grid[i] * LHAIRD_base
  LHAIRV <- condition_grid[i] * LHAIRV_base
  RHOD   <- condition_grid[i] * RHOD_base
  RHOV   <- condition_grid[i] * RHOV_base

  ZFURD_MAX <- LHAIRD
  ZFURV_MAX <-LHAIRV

  # Run endoR across all microclimate time steps
  endo.out <- lapply(seq_along(TAs), function(x) {

    TORPOR <- if (Zs[x] >= 90) 1 else 0

    # Run endoR with modified insulation
    endoR(
      # Climate variables
      TA = TAs[x], TAREF = TAREFs[x], TSKY = TSKYs[x], TGRD = TGRDs[x],
      VEL = VELs[x], RH = RHs[x], QSOLR = QSOLRs[x], Z = Zs[x], ELEV = ELEV,
      ABSSB = ABSSB,

      # Morphometrics
      AMASS = AMASS, ANDENS = ANDENS, AK1 = AK1, SHAPE_B = SHAPE_B,
      SHAPE_B_MAX = SHAPE_B_MAX, UNCURL = UNCURL, SHAPE = SHAPE,
      SAMODE = SAMODE, FATPCT = FATPCT,

      # Metabolic Parameters
      TC = TC, TC_MAX = TC_MAX, TC_MIN = TC_MIN,TC_INC = TC_INC,
      PCTWET = PCTWET, PCTWET_MAX = PCTWET_MAX, PCTWET_INC = PCTWET_INC,
      Q10 = Q10s[x], QBASAL = QBASAL, DELTAR = DELTAR, EXTREF = EXTREF,
      PANT_INC = PANT_INC, PANT_MAX = PANT_MAX, PANT_MULT = PANT_MULT,
      TORPOR = TORPOR, # Torpor is the main addition to nighttime runs

      # Fixed Feather Properties
      DHAIRD = DHAIRD, DHAIRV = DHAIRV, REFLD = REFLD, REFLV = REFLV,

      # Varied Feather Properties
      ZFURD_MAX = ZFURD_MAX, ZFURV_MAX = ZFURV_MAX,

      LHAIRD = LHAIRD, LHAIRV = LHAIRV,

      RHOD = RHOD, RHOV = RHOV, TREGMODE = TREGMODE,

    )
  })

  # Convert list of endoR outputs into a single data frame
  endo_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(endo.out, data.frame))

  # Climate

  daynight <- ifelse(Zs >= 90, "torpid_night", "day")

  # Extract heat balance (metabolic rate)
  enbal <- endo_df[, grep("enbal", colnames(endo_df))]
  colnames(enbal) <- gsub("enbal.", "", colnames(enbal))

  # Thermoregulation output
  treg <- endo_df[, grep("treg", colnames(endo_df))]
  colnames(treg) <- gsub("treg\\.", "", colnames(treg))

  # Mass aspects
  masbal <- endo_df[, grep("masbal", colnames(endo_df))]
  colnames(masbal) <- gsub("masbal\\.", "", colnames(masbal))

  # Save results for this condition level

  results_list_torpor[[i]] <- data.frame(

    condition = condition_grid[i],
    time_step = seq_along(TAs),
    QGEN = enbal$QGEN,                             # Metabolic energy generated
    TCs = treg$TC,                                 # Core temperature
    H2O = masbal$H2OResp_g + masbal$H2OCut_g,      # Water evaporated (g/hour)
    TFA_D = treg$TFA_D,                            # Dorsal fur surface temperature
    TFA_V = treg$TFA_V,                            # Ventral fur surface temperature
    TskinD = treg$TSKIN_D,                         # Dorsal skin temperature
    TskinV = treg$TSKIN_V,                         # Ventral skin temperature
    Pant = treg$PANT,                              # Panting multiplier
    daynight = daynight                            # Day or night
  )
}

proc.time() - ptm

results_all_torpor <- do.call(rbind, results_list_torpor)

sanity_check <- subset(results_all_torpor, condition == 1)

ggplot(sanity_check, aes(x = time_step)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = TFA_D, color = "Feathers dorsal", linetype = "Feathers dorsal")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = TFA_V, color = "Feathers ventral", linetype = "Feathers ventral")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = TskinD, color = "Skin dorsal", linetype = "Skin dorsal")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = TskinV, color = "Skin ventral", linetype = "Skin ventral")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = TCs, color = "Core", linetype = "Core")) +
  geom_line(aes(y=TAs, color = "Air Temperature", linetype = "Air Temperature")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Core" = "red", "Skin dorsal" = "orange", "Skin ventral" = "orange", "Feathers dorsal" = "darkgreen",
                                "Feathers ventral"= "darkgreen", "Air Temperature" = "violet")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Core" = 1, "Skin dorsal" = 1, "Skin ventral" = 2, "Feathers dorsal" = 1,
                                   "Feathers ventral"= 2, "Air Temperature" = 1)) +
  labs(x = "time", y = "temperature (°C)", color = "", linetype = "") +
  ylim(-10, 50) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.key.width = unit(1.5, "cm")
  )
########################################################################

messages.body_plain:
Hi Mike,

I am now making some simulations for males and females, using male specific parameters (in fact, individual level parameters) as you suggested.

The problem is that the "reproductive strategy" is the same for females/males (using batch=1 and abclutch), so the males don't use the energy stored in the reproduction buffer some years because they are unable to produce a clutch... However, I would expect males to deplete the reproduction buffer each year, fertilizing more or less eggs, depending on how much energy they have stored. Is it possible to simulate that?

Thanks a lot in advance!

Cheers,

Urtzi
